scenes.title: Browser workshop
scenes.description: Customize a browser, stop a tracking signal, then use Inspect to change its visible style.

scenes.title: Our side of the doorway
scenes.description: Our handle opens onto nature, architecture and a digital world. A purposeful push ends in an illustrative matched cut, not a geometric morph.

views.name: Door opens onto a connected world

scenes.title: The final say
scenes.description: Return to the same editable browser controls; the user keeps the final choice.

rhythm.method: Time/frequency median masks suppress sustained harmonic energy; positive log spectral flux weighted 70% at 40–180Hz and 30% at 2–8kHz; median-baseline removal; autocorrelation 75–187 BPM and phase search; onset snap within 75ms. Not source separation: vocal transients can remain. Interpolated beats do not drive default accents.

browserHistory.title: Netscape source → Mozilla
browserHistory.label: Source released → Mozilla
browserHistory.note: March 31, 1998: Netscape source release; not the Firefox launch. Hardware illustrates eras, not invention dates.

browserHistory.title: Safari beta
browserHistory.label: Safari · WebKit inside
browserHistory.note: Safari beta January 7, 2003; Safari 1.0 June 23. Safari is a browser product; WebKit is its open-source engine. This does not classify privacy or connection security.

browserHistory.title: Firefox 1.0
browserHistory.label: Firefox · open-source browser
browserHistory.note: Firefox 1.0 released November 9, 2004. Present-day controls are an illustrative openness demonstration, not a reconstruction of the historical UI.

browserHistory.title: Chrome beta + Chromium
browserHistory.label: Chrome · built on Chromium
browserHistory.note: Chrome beta and Chromium launched September 2, 2008. Chrome builds on open-source Chromium and adds proprietary components. No lock implies privacy, security, or a wholly closed engine.
